name: East Buttress

pitch_detail.notes: Lower buttress, scrambling terrain on solid granite.
Class 5 climbing close to the crest, working under overhangs on sound rock; original ascent used occasional aid pitons, later freed at 5.10.

approach: Approach as for the East Ridge/Hardscrabble Route: walk/bike the gated Middle Fork Snoqualmie River Road to the Hardscrabble Lakes boot path, then continue to lower Hardscrabble Lake. Traverse the lake's left (north) side and scramble two rock bands to reach the buttress's south side at roughly 5,400 ft.
overview: A 10-pitch line on the crest of Big Snow Mountain's East Buttress above lower Hardscrabble Lake, a buttress marked by a prominent dihedral and overhangs. Traverse the left side of the lake and scramble two rock bands to the south side of the buttress at about 5,400 ft, then stay close to the crest, working under overhangs from a southern to a northern exposure on very sound granite: four pitches of class 4, then class 5 with a few aid placements.
beta: From lower Hardscrabble Lake, traverse its left (north) side and scramble over two rock bands to reach the south side of the buttress at about 5,400 ft. Climb close to the crest of the buttress, working under overhangs, on generally solid granite for 10 pitches (originally 4 pitches of class 4 followed by class 5 climbing with occasional aid pitons) to the summit area.
fa: Jeff Dial and Don Williamson, May 11, 1971 (NCCS III, 5.7, A1)
